interest: Refugee price data from the Changchun siege and Ward's debate on keeping the Mukden consulate open, 1948.
overview: Angus Ward's despatch of October 21, 1948 sends Siebens' memo on starvation prices in fallen Changchun and warns Mukden faces the same fate under siege.

subfiles.about: Covering despatch transmitting Vice Consul Siebens' memorandum on Changchun's cost of living and evaluating the feasibility of maintaining the Mukden Consulate General under an anticipated Communist siege.
subfiles.from: Angus Ward, U.S. Consul General, Mukden
subfiles.summary: Angus Ward forwards Siebens' memorandum on Changchun's collapse after eighteen months of siege. He warns that a besieged Mukden would lose food and coal, and asks whether the Consulate General can stay open through spring 1949.
subfiles.title: Despatch from Consul General Angus Ward transmitting memorandum on Changchun and Mukden economic situations

subfiles.about: Intelligence memorandum analyzing refugee price data from besieged Changchun and forecasting a parallel collapse of utilities, currency, and living conditions in Mukden.
subfiles.from: Allen C. Siebens, American Vice Consul, Mukden
subfiles.summary: Siebens uses refugee reports to tabulate Changchun's siege prices in September 1948 and warns that Mukden faces the same inflation, with power, coal and water vulnerable to Communist cutoff at Fushun and Benxi.
subfiles.title: Memorandum by Vice Consul Allen C. Siebens on cost of living at Changchun and anticipated duplication at Mukden
